title: XGBoost model predicts 2-year metabolic syndrome risk under simulated weight targets
summary: Using 3,447 Ansan and 3,874 Anseong participants of the Korean Genome and Epidemiology Study, models were trained on 70% of Ansan participants, internally validated on 30%, and externally validated on all 15,739 Anseong observations. XGBoost outperformed logistic regression, Gaussian naive Bayes, random forest and a deep neural network (AUC 0.879) with better calibration. The model was built into an application that simulates 2-year metabolic syndrome probability at target body weights. Whether weight-control programs improve outcomes still needs prospective study.
ai_technology: XGBoost prediction model compared with logistic regression, random forest, naive Bayes and a deep neural network
organization: Yonsei University; Wonju Severance Christian Hospital; Yonsei University Mirae Campus

evidence.tested: Internal validation in 30% of the Ansan cohort and external validation in the Anseong cohort.
evidence.unknown: Whether following simulated weight targets reduces metabolic syndrome; full text not reviewed.
